shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Default card/panel elevation in light theme; in dark theme depth relies on surface/bg contrast instead.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Hover lift on interactive cards and the sticky header once scrolled.

narrative.overview:
OnlyPing is redesigned around the one line that structures every ping-pong table: the center line. The product becomes a clean, well-lit, structured surface — closer to a modern sport-tech SaaS dashboard than the previous dim graphite room — because the audience is not just spectators, it's players and coaches doing a job (browsing, buying, publishing, managing payouts). Structure and legibility lead; energy is reserved for one color.

That one color is a competition-ball orange: Accent. Everything else is quiet — neutral surfaces, a calm navy-black ink, soft dividing lines — so that price tags, primary actions, and active states read instantly as "the thing to do here." Light and dark are both first-class: the same structure, ink and accent hold in both, only the surface/background values invert.
keyCharacteristics: Structured, editorial-grade neutrals with a true light theme and a true dark theme, switchable by the user.
One saturated accent — competition-ball orange — spent only on price, primary actions, and active/selected states.
Soft, restrained elevation (gentle shadows on cards) instead of flat borders alone.
Geometric display type (Space Grotesk) over a neutral, highly-legible body face (Inter) — professional, not playful.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange marks the single decisive element per view: a price, the primary CTA, an active tab/filter, a focus ring. If two elements compete for it, one loses the accent.

rules.name: The Invert, Don't Recolor Rule
rules.body: Moving between light and dark never changes which token a component uses — only what bg/surface/ink resolve to.

rules.name: The Quiet Lift Rule
rules.body: Elevation communicates interactivity, not decoration: only elements a user can act on lift on hover.

dos: Do spend Accent on exactly one decisive element per view — The One Accent Rule.
Do author every component against the semantic tokens so it inverts correctly between light and dark automatically.
Do give interactive cards a hover lift; keep static panels at Resting.
donts: Don't reintroduce the previous graphite/gold palette or the flat-only, border-as-only-depth system.
Don't use Accent for category chips or status tags; they stay in their own quiet tint family.
Don't hardcode a hex color in a component; every color must resolve through a semantic token.
